english: At first the night wasn’t quite coming together.
Then more people arrived.
The groups mixed.
And then it really came together.
It changed loads.

foreign: En un momento el ambiente se puso raro.
english: At one point the atmosphere got weird.

foreign: No sé muy bien por qué.
english: I’m not exactly sure why.
There wasn’t a big argument.
Something just shifted.
You could feel tension.

foreign: Y veinte minutos después volvió a estar todo normal.
english: And twenty minutes later everything was normal again.

foreign: No sé si hablaron entre ellos.
english: I don’t know if they spoke privately.
Or if it just passed.
But the atmosphere relaxed.

foreign: Yo me perdí toda la parte rara.
english: I missed the entire weird bit.
I was outside talking to someone.

foreign: Volví y noté que había cambiado el ambiente.
english: I came back and noticed the atmosphere had changed.
I asked what had happened.
And everyone said, “Later.”
Then nobody told me.

foreign: Tuve que preguntar al día siguiente.
english: I had to ask the next day.

foreign: Y aun así recibí tres versiones distintas.
english: And even then I got three different versions.

foreign: Así que sigo sin saber exactamente qué pasó.
english: So I still don’t know exactly what happened.

foreign: Por eso una cena de cuatro horas puede generar veinte historias.
english: That’s why a four-hour dinner can generate twenty stories.

foreign: No está pasando una sola cosa.
english: There isn’t just one thing happening.
There are parallel conversations.
People arriving and leaving.
Misunderstandings.
Coincidences.

foreign: Y pequeños momentos que luego cuentas durante años.
english: And little moments you then tell for years.

foreign: Y la mitad te enteras después.
english: And you only find out about half of it afterwards.
“What do you mean that happened?”
“Where was I?”
“You were there.”
“Well, I saw none of it.”
“But you were right next to us.”

foreign: Aparentemente estaba en mi propio mundo.
english: Apparently I was in my own world.
I processed absolutely nothing.
That happens too.
“I thought you already knew.”
Nope.
Nobody had told me anything.

foreign: Todo el mundo había asumido que otra persona me lo había contado.
english: Everyone had assumed someone else had told me.
Classic.
“Okay, now I want to know everything.”
“From the beginning.”
“Who was there?”
“Who said what?”
“And how did it end?”
A full investigation begins.

foreign: A veces la historia no está completa hasta el día siguiente.
english: Sometimes the story isn’t complete until the next day.
When you speak to several people.
You see photos.
You read messages.
And you put it all together.

foreign: Ahí ya tienes la versión definitiva.
english: Then you have the definitive version.
Or the closest thing to it.

foreign: El lunes la historia ya tiene estructura.
english: By Monday the story has structure.
On Saturday it was just chaos.
Sunday is when reconstruction starts.

foreign: Y el lunes ya tienes principio, nudo y desenlace.
english: And by Monday you have a beginning, middle and end.

foreign: Además cada vez que la cuentas aprendes dónde hacer la pausa.
english: Plus, every time you tell it you learn where to pause.
Which details are unnecessary.
Which line matters.
And where the punchline is.

foreign: A la quinta vez ya es una obra pulida.
english: By the fifth telling it’s a polished work.

foreign: La primera vez que cuentas algo suele ser fatal.
english: The first time you tell something it’s often terrible.

foreign: Te acuerdas de cosas fuera de orden.
english: You remember things out of order.
You add context too late.
You correct yourself.

foreign: Y la otra persona tiene que hacer un esfuerzo para seguirte.
english: And the other person has to make an effort to follow you.
But that’s how we really talk.

foreign: No contamos historias como si estuviéramos escribiendo un libro.
english: We don’t tell stories as though we’re writing a book.
We remember as we speak.
And the listener participates too.
They ask questions.
They react.
They correct you.
And they add their own story.

foreign: Y luego tu historia le recuerda una suya.
english: And then your story reminds them of one of theirs.
They start telling it.
Your story remains unfinished.

foreign: Veinte minutos después alguien dice: “Espera, ¿y qué pasó con lo tuyo?”
english: Twenty minutes later someone says, “Wait, what happened with your thing?”
And we return.
That’s how one anecdote generates another.
And another.
And another.

foreign: Y de repente llevas dos horas hablando.
english: And suddenly you’ve been talking for two hours.

foreign: Sin haber vuelto al tema original.
english: Without having returned to the original topic.
Brilliant.
I love this story.
This is brilliant.
No way.
This is too much.
Amazing.
This feels scripted.
You couldn’t do that deliberately.
You can’t make this stuff up.
What bad luck.
Everything just came together at once.
There wasn’t much you could do.
How exhausting.
I’m tired just hearing it.
What a day.
What a night.
You were so lucky.
Thank goodness.
By the skin of your teeth.

foreign: Eso fue el universo echándoos una mano.
english: That was the universe giving you a hand.
It worked out perfectly for you.
It worked out so well in the end.
I’d have a heart attack.
I’d die on the spot.
How stressful.
I don’t even want to imagine it.

foreign: Menos mal que te diste cuenta.
english: Thank goodness you noticed.
Thank goodness you checked.
Thank goodness you went back.

foreign: Eso me pasaría a mí perfectamente.
english: That could absolutely happen to me.
That’s very on-brand for me.

foreign: Me estoy riendo, pero porque me veo haciéndolo.
english: I’m laughing because I can see myself doing it.

foreign: No tengo autoridad moral para juzgarte.
english: I have no moral authority to judge you.

foreign: Es que a mí me ha pasado exactamente eso.
english: That exact thing has happened to me.
Wait, I’ll tell you.

foreign: Lo mío fue todavía más absurdo.
english: Mine was even more absurd.
Not that we’re competing.
But listen.
And now we have another story.
This never ends.
One story calls forth another.

foreign: Es básicamente el motor de una cena larga.
english: It’s basically the engine of a long dinner.

foreign: Y nada, al final fue una noche buenísima.
english: And yeah, in the end it was a brilliant night.

foreign: Mucho más divertida de lo que esperaba.
english: Much more fun than I expected.

foreign: Con bastante más drama del necesario.
english: With quite a bit more drama than necessary.
But everything ended well.

foreign: Así que ahora solo quedan las historias.
english: So now all that’s left are the stories.
I wouldn’t repeat the logistics.
But I’d repeat the plan.
With a few changes.
And perhaps a list.

foreign: Una lista que esta vez sí miraríamos.
english: A list we’d actually look at this time.

foreign: Y eso fue lo cerca que estuvimos de liarla.
english: And that’s how close we came to messing it up.
Nothing happened in the end.
But for five minutes…
I can’t even tell you.
Now it’s funny.

foreign: Y si no hubiera pasado esa primera tontería, nada de lo demás habría pasado.
english: And if that first tiny thing hadn’t happened, none of the rest would’ve happened.

foreign: Eso es lo que me parece curioso.
english: That’s what I find interesting.
It wasn’t an important decision.
But it changed the whole sequence.

foreign: En fin, una noche muy normal que acabó no siendo nada normal.
english: Anyway, a very normal night that ended up not being normal at all.
We started with a quiet dinner.

foreign: Y acabamos con veinte personas y tres grupos mezclados.
english: And ended up with twenty people and three groups merged together.
It wasn’t planned.
But it was great.

foreign: Y otras veces vas sin expectativas y acaba siendo simplemente agradable.
english: And other times you go in with no expectations and it just ends up being nice.
Without any huge story.
Without drama.
Without a final twist.
Just a good night.

foreign: Pero claro, luego alguien dice: “¿Qué tal ayer?”
english: But of course, then someone asks, “How was yesterday?”

foreign: Y tú dices: “Bien… aunque pasó una cosa.”
english: And you say, “Good… although one thing happened.”

foreign: Y ya hemos vuelto a empezar.
english: And there we are starting all over again.
